newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian rebel city sad Vranitzky cancelled trip.
newsitem.headline: Albanian rebel city sad Vranitzky cancelled trip.

text.p: Residents of this Albanian rebel-held city, who had expected a visit by international mediator Franz Vranitzky, said on Thursday they were greatly disappointed by the cancellation of his trip.
"We are disappointed. We invited him and we had a lot of problems to discuss with him. But we expect him to come (on a future visit)," Gjergji Muco, a leader of the rebel committee, told Reuters.
"The reason he did not come might be a conflict he had with (President Sali) Berisha, but we do not think that the future of Vraniztky's mission is in danger," he added.

Rebels seized control of the south earlier this year. They blame Berisha for the pyramid schemes which cost many Albanians their savings. Nearly 300 were killed in unchecked violence after people looted arsenals deserted by police and troops.
Albanian newspapers said Vranitzky, mediator for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), and Berisha had argued during a meeting in Tirana on Wednesday.
Vranitzky cancelled a trip to Vlore in the south scheduled for Thursday, saying he wanted to hold further meetings in Tirana to focus on general elections planned for June.
Medin Xhelili, head of the regional council in Vlore, said he was disappointed Vranitzky had cancelled his trip and said Berisha was to blame for the last-minute decision.
"Berisha is plotting against the government and its spirit of reconciliation," Xhelili told Reuters.
Rebel committee sources said several thousand people in Vlore had been expected to welcome Vranitzky on Thursday.
Last Sunday at least 10,000 local people feted italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi who came to express Italy's determination to help Albania to overcome its crisis.
"We were prepared to receive him in the same manner Prodi was welcomed," said Thanas Haluci, a rebel committee member.
He said Berisha had probably told Vranitzky that the government could not guarantee the security of the former Austrian chancellor.
But Vranitzky, speaking in Tirana, said that security was only a secondary reason he stayed in Tirana on Thursday.

"Aside from the fact that I was told it is not entirely safe, the main reason (the trip was cancelled is because) I had, am having and will have a number of conversations concerning the preparations for the elections," Vranitzky said.
Local residents of Vlore said they were saddened when Vranitzky called off his trip.

"People are concerned about Vranitzky's failure to come because he was one of the first to talk to the rebel committees. They are afraid he might have teamed up with Berisha," said Shpresa Nelaj, 40, a greengrocer.
Pelivan Sulo, a 50-year-old mechanic, said: "His failure to come is like driving a nail into us because we had expected him with much hope."
A shop assistant said she had prepared a bouquet of flowers for Vranitzky's visit.
